title: Oil price dives as US and Iran pause attacks
facts: Brent crude oil dropped over 9% to reach $87.59 per barrel following a temporary pause in military strikes.
Brent crude had traded above $100 per barrel during the previous week.
The US ambassador to the United Nations stated that attacks on Iran were halted for two consecutive nights.
An Iranian military spokesperson announced that Tehran halted retaliatory attacks across the region.
The Strait of Hormuz typically carries approximately 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.
The United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June to temporarily halt military operations.
Brent crude oil prices had fallen to roughly $70 per barrel following the June memorandum of understanding.
Houthi militia forces in Yemen conducted attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea.
Susannah Streeter serves as chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
A research report by Wood Mackenzie indicated European gas storage levels had reached historic lows.
Wood Mackenzie projected European gas storage would fall below 70% by November 1 if the Strait of Hormuz remained closed for two more months.
The five-year average for European gas storage levels on November 1 is 90%.
Massimo Di Odoardo serves as vice president of gas and LNG research at Wood Mackenzie.
The European Central Bank raised its benchmark interest rate for the eurozone in June.
The Bank of England held its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75%.
